$comment: Protocol coverage manifest (Inc 1 of docs/design/protocol-contract.md). Every schema exported by the vendored gateway-protocol modules (protocol/openclaw/<version>/) must be classified here — either whole-schema or field-by-field. The ratchet test (test/protocol-coverage.test.ts) walks the vendored TypeBox schemas and fails on any unclassified schema/field, so a validated-version bump that introduces new protocol surface stays RED until a human classifies it. statuses: handled (consumed/emitted by the bridge, `by` = where) | ignored (deliberate, `why` required) | gap (known-unsupported, `note` required). Seeded from the audit in docs/design/protocol-schema-coverage.md.

firstKeptEntryId.why: transcript-internal cursor with no meaning outside the gateway's own store

preCompaction.why: transcript reference (see SessionCompactionTranscriptReference) — file-level pointers into the gateway's disk, unusable and unwanted here

SessionCompactionCheckpointReason.why: the reason vocabulary as a union. The bridge does not match this union: it BUCKETS the reason string it receives (bucketCompactionReason) at both the history shaper and the trace boundary, so a new upstream member collapses to `other` instead of breaking a turn or travelling verbatim onto a metadata-only surface. NOTE: that bucketing was ADDED on 2026-07-27 — classifying this schema is what revealed the history shaper was still passing the raw string through.

sessionFile.why: a PATH on the gateway host — never useful to Atrium and never safe to surface

operationId.note: NOT RECEIVED. This event reaches only connections that called `sessions.subscribe`, which the bridge deliberately does NOT do on the turn socket (measured 2026-07-26: subscribing there cost announce frames and broke turn merging). Reading it needs a dedicated connection; `handleSessionOperation` in the normalizer is the ready, unfed reader.

operation.note: same: unfed until the dedicated session-events connection exists

reason.note: same — and this is the field that matters. CORRECTED after review: it is not the ONLY carrier of a compaction cause, as this note first claimed. `sessions.compaction.list` returns checkpoints whose `reason` the bridge already reads (fetchCompactionHistory), so the cause IS retrievable ON DEMAND, per session, off the turn path. What this event alone would give is the cause AT THE MOMENT it happens, attachable to the turn's own marker and trace, instead of a later lookup nobody performs.

reason.note: NOT sent, and CORRECTED after review: the first note claimed sending it would let the gateway's audit tell an Atrium reset from any other. It would not — the schema admits only `"new" | "reset"`, so every client's reset looks alike. What sending `"reset"` would actually buy is the distinction from `"new"` (a fresh session) inside the gateway's own lifecycle accounting. Minor, and Atrium keeps its own reset trace either way.

CronPayload.by: normalizeCronJobDetail reads `kind` (the payload family the message editor must preserve) and the prompt text — `message` for an agentTurn, `text` for a systemEvent. A UNION, so it is classified whole: the bridge reads the members' shared fields rather than matching the union, and an unknown member degrades to a null prompt instead of breaking the detail.

CronPayloadPatch.by: buildGatewayCronPatch SENDS one: editing a cron's prompt emits `{kind:"systemEvent", text}` or `{kind:"agentTurn", message}`, chosen from the job's CURRENT kind. An unknown current kind fails CLOSED (the update is refused) rather than guessing a member.
